correctness.rationale: Exact antipodal angle variables theta1=phi-v/2, theta2=phi+pi+v/2 give D=2a cos(v/2)sqrt(1-delta sin^2(phi)) with Jacobian one and product arclength density. For fixed 0<delta<1 the two nondegenerate maxima yield F ~ pi(1-delta)epsilon/(4a E(delta)^2 sqrt(delta)); for the circle, the exact arccos law has sqrt epsilon tail. For delta/(epsilon/a)->lambda finite, dominated convergence after v=2sqrt(epsilon/a)u gives H(lambda)=pi^-2 integral sqrt((1-lambda sin^2 phi)_+)dphi. Piecewise complete elliptic formula and DLMF endpoint series give pi^2 H(1+h)=4+h log|h|+(1-log16)h+O(h^2|log h|). Independently checked both branches of H with high-precision quadrature and two-sided cusp coefficients. The large-lambda asymptotic is not falsely used as a uniform theorem for delta/epsilon->infinity.
